# Original synthetic contract lesson

An inner join returns matching row pairs. A join condition states how table columns correspond.
A left outer join preserves each row of its left table even without a right-side match.
Unmatched right-side attributes become NULL. A missing foreign-key value and an unmatched non-NULL reference are different cases.
Use a null predicate on an appropriate joined key to reason about missing matches. Filtering after a join can remove preserved rows.

This paragraph is an original test fixture, not a UIUC lecture, extracted PDF, or research result.
